title: Completed stalks and the closed fibre of a flat finite type morphism
statement: Let $f:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $t\in T$, $s=f(t)$, $A_0=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and $B_0=\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Suppose $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and flat at $t$ [def-weil-flat-morphism], $A_0$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and the induced map of residue fields $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. Put $k=\kappa(s)$, $A=\widehat{A_0}$, $B=\widehat{B_0}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_{A_0}A$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_{B_0}B$, using maximal-ideal-adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $B_0$ is Noetherian; $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian local rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak n$, respectively, and both residue fields are canonically $k$. The induced map $A\to B$ is local and flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $A$ and $B$ are complete for their respective maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Writing $T_s$ for the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and $t_s$ for its point over $t$, there is a canonical $k$-algebra isomorphism $B/\mathfrak mB\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{T_s,t_s}$ compatible with the quotient map from $B_0$ and with completion.

proof.text: Put $\varphi=f_t^\sharp:A_0\to B_0$. It is local because a scheme morphism is a morphism of locally ringed spaces, and flat by the hypothesis of flatness at $t$. The stalk finite-type lemma says that $B_0$ is a localization of a finite-type $A_0$-algebra $C$. Since $A_0$ is Noetherian, $C$ is Noetherian by finite-type Noetherian permanence, and its localization $B_0$ is Noetherian by localization permanence.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family, first proof paragraph; the local Noetherianity reduction.

proof.text: Apply Noetherianity of adic completion to $A_0$ and $B_0$. Apply the local-completion lemma to each: $A$ and $B$ are local with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_{A_0}A$ and $\mathfrak m_{B_0}B$, and their residue fields identify with those of $A_0$ and $B_0$. The given residue-field isomorphism therefore identifies both with $k$. Their maximal ideals before completion are finitely generated by the definition of Noetherianity. The completion-mod-ideal lemma then makes $A$ and $B$ complete for the displayed extended maximal ideals.

Apply the flat-completion lemma to the flat local map $\varphi$ between the now Noetherian local rings $A_0,B_0$. It gives the canonical flat map $\widehat\varphi:A\to B$, characterized coordinatewise by $a\bmod\mathfrak m_{A_0}^r\mapsto\varphi(a)\bmod\mathfrak m_{B_0}^r$. This map is local: every generator from $\mathfrak m_{A_0}$ maps into $\mathfrak m_{B_0}B$, so $\widehat\varphi(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$. The induced residue map is the original residue-field isomorphism, as is seen from coordinate $r=1$.

Let $D=\mathcal O_{T_s,t_s}$ and let $q:B_0\to D$ be the fibre projection stalk map. The scheme-fibre stalk quotient lemma says that $q$ is surjective with kernel $J=\mathfrak m_{A_0}B_0$. It is local, so it maps $\mathfrak m_{B_0}$ onto the maximal ideal of $D$; indeed the inverse image of that maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_{B_0}$, and $q$ is onto. Apply the local-completion quotient lemma to this surjection. It gives a ring isomorphism $B/JB\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat D$, induced by the coordinatewise completed map $\widehat q$, satisfying $\widehat q\circ\iota_{B_0}=\iota_D\circ q$.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family, first paragraph, fibre quotient; Schemes Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre) and Algebra Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor).

proof.text: The ideals $JB$ and $\mathfrak mB$ are equal: both are generated in $B$ by the image of $\mathfrak m_{A_0}$, since $J=\mathfrak m_{A_0}B_0$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_{A_0}A$. Thus the previous isomorphism has source $B/\mathfrak mB$. It is a $k$-algebra map for $k=A_0/\mathfrak m_{A_0}=A/\mathfrak m$: a class in $k$ has a representative $a\in A_0$, and the commuting equality for $\widehat q$ sends its action on $1$ to the image of $q(\varphi(a))$ in $\widehat D$. This is exactly the coefficient action from the fibre projection to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. At level $r$, the map is $B_0/\mathfrak m_{B_0}^r\to D/\mathfrak m_D^r$, $b\mapsto q(b)$; these maps commute with all quotient transitions. This proves both the asserted compatibility with the quotient from $B_0$ and the compatibility with completion.
